answer: A spiral staircase of escrowed trust. A newcomer locks a $120 bond and registers one key on a basalt ledger. Steps run 3, 6, 12, then 24 client jobs, each signed by its client and posted openly. At each step two random established peers re-run one job; one forged result drops the climber to step zero, burns the $120 bond, bans the key 90 days. Finish 45 jobs in 60 days and the bond returns with a jade seal. Faking 1,000 identities costs $120,000 plus 45,000 real jobs, about 11,250 hours. Trust is a lighthouse stair cut in basalt: every step earned, one slip and you start at the rocks.
